root_cause.text: In the ptrace SVE write path in `sve_set_common()`, the code that sets the TIF_SVE thread flag was incorrectly guarded by a `system_supports_sme()` check, so on systems with SVE but without SME, TIF_SVE was not set when writing SVE-formatted state, leaving the task in an inconsistent state (FP_STATE_SVE format but TIF_SVE clear), which later triggered a warning.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "This bug was introduced during rework to error handling in commit 9f8bf718f2923 ... where the setting of TIF_SVE was moved into a block which is only executed when system_supports_sme() is true." The patch diff removes the `if (system_supports_sme())` guard around the switch that sets TIF_SVE/TIF_SME, ensuring TIF_SVE is always set for SVE writes.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove unnecessary system_supports_sme() guard to allow SVE state to be set on systems without SME support.
intent_record.what: Removed the outer if (system_supports_sme()) condition that wrapped the switch statement for setting streaming mode flags.
intent_record.how: Previously, the SVCR and thread flag updates for SVE and SME modes only executed when the system supported SME. After the change, the switch executes unconditionally, allowing SVE state to be set correctly even on systems without SME, while SME operations still fail gracefully via the default case.

vuln_statements.explanation: This guard incorrectly restricts the setting of TIF_SVE to only when SME is supported, so on systems with SVE but without SME (or where SVE is enabled but SME is not), the TIF_SVE flag is not set when writing SVE-formatted state. This leaves the task in an inconsistent state (FP_STATE_SVE format but TIF_SVE clear), triggering a warning later.

bic_trace_step.reason: In sve_set_common(), the TIF_SVE flag is set unconditionally (line `set_tsk_thread_flag(target, TIF_SVE);`) after handling the FPSIMD-only case. There is no guard by `system_supports_sme()` that would prevent setting it on non-SME systems. Therefore, the vulnerable construct described in the root cause (incorrectly guarding the TIF_SVE set with an SME check) is absent in this commit.
